name: Merit Shaw
life: Merit's first forwarding job was sending home a dead sailor's boots. She learned that a parcel can arrive before a family is ready to open it. Her quotations include a space for the recipient to choose a date. On Thursday, near Juniper Street, Merit knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I offered to pay to ship it to his sister. Then I learned they haven't spoken in eleven years. I gave him the quote in a sealed envelope he can throw away.
appearance: Merit has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a rust-colored canvas coat with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Merit turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Merit always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Merit is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To leave the sister free to decline both the chair and the reconciliation.
family: Adriana Arnett is Merit’s half-sibling. Merit puts the kettle on. Adriana chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The second dog*, Adriana says, “I have the delivery photo of both dogs in the same yard.”
connections: Nell Oram. The shipping quote and the recorded recollections are the only things the absent sister can receive without taking ownership.

reactions.response: Merit asks each claimant what they remember about the seat before the marks are shown.
